title: NYC Daily Digest
text:
☀️ Good morning, Matthew! It's Tuesday, November 3, 2026, Election Day.

🌤️ Weather
Mostly sunny and mild. It starts cool this morning and warms to a high of about 67–69°F, near 70 in spots. No real rain is expected today, so there's 0% to worry about. Heads-up: a possible soaker arrives Thursday night into Friday.
What to wear: a light jacket you can take off by noon and sunglasses. Leave the umbrella at home.

🗞️ Headlines
• Midterms today: Control of the House and Senate is at stake. The economy and the Iran war top voters' concerns. More than 57 million Americans voted early, and some races may not be called tonight.
• Iran: The U.S. carried out what it called "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired on a U.S. aircraft. Iran says three tankers hit mines in the strait. Talks continue, and Trump says a deal is still possible.
• NY governor: Gov. Hochul is running for a second full term against Republican Bruce Blakeman. Final polls gave her a double-digit lead (Siena: 54–40). Over 690K NYC voters already cast ballots early.
• The DOJ is sending a record number of election monitors to all 50 states. Separately, the Supreme Court rejected a Trump administration appeal over 20,000 California mail ballots.
• Storms elsewhere: Flooding and tornadoes forced some polling places to move in three regions of the country, including parts of Florida.

🚇 Getting around
I didn't find any major planned subway changes for today. Expect busier streets and stations near polling sites, and check the MTA app before you head out.

🎉 NYC today
• 🗳️ Polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. You can look up your polling site at the NYC Board of Elections site (findmypollsite.vote.nyc). Expect results to start coming in after 9 p.m.
• 🍂 It's one of the last near-70° days of the season, so a lunchtime walk in the park or along the waterfront is a good idea.

💡 Nugget
In New York you can vote at your assigned polling site even if you're in line when polls close at 9 p.m. If you're in line by 9, stay in line. Bring a book, not a phone at 2%.
